sources.title: HubSpot pricing 2026 – what does the new model mean?
sources.snippet_text:
| 8 min read

HubSpot pricing is changing in 2026. The change affects licences and how the overall CRM setup should be built. However, the new pricing model only applies to new HubSpot implementations.

HubSpot has renewed its pricing with the Flexible Seats-and-Credits model. In it, the Customer Platform is purchased at the Starter, Pro or Enterprise level, users are assigned seats based on their tasks, and parts of system usage consume HubSpot Credits. [...] In the Flexible Seats-and-Credits model, you do not pay for marketing contacts according to a separate Marketing Contacts tier. Instead, the account has a record capacity based on the selected edition.

Starter has a capacity of 25,000 records, Pro 250,000 and Enterprise 15 million. The limit applies to the relevant CRM objects as a whole. In addition to contacts, companies, deals and tickets, for example, are also counted. [...] HubSpot has renamed the seats in the new pricing model. Previously, the names Front Office Seat and Core Seat were used. With the update, the paid seats have been named GTM Seat and Ops Seat.

The GTM Seat is intended for users who work directly with customers. This includes, for example, marketing, sales and customer service. According to HubSpot, the GTM Seat provides access to the marketing, sales and service features at the relevant edition level.

sources.snippet_text:
A side project with scale-to-zero can cost as little as $1–3/month. A production SaaS on 1 CU always-on runs about $78/month before storage. Neon has no monthly minimum on the Launch plan — you pay only for what you use.

### Does Neon have a free plan?

Yes. The Free plan includes 100 CU-hours/month, 0.5 GB storage, and up to 2 CU autoscale. It is suitable for development and side projects. The Launch plan removes these limits and enables scale-to-zero with configurable autoscale up to 8 CU. [...] ## How Neon pricing works in 2026

Neon is a serverless Postgres database with two distinct billing dimensions: compute and storage. Compute is measured in Compute Units (CU) — one CU equals 1 vCPU and 4 GB RAM — and billed per hour of active use at $0.106/CU-hour on the Launch plan. Storage is $0.35/GB-month. Egress is 100 GB/month included, then $0.10/GB. [...] Billing is based on the CU size at each moment, not a fixed tier. If your database only spikes to 2 CU for 2 hours out of the month, you pay for 2 CU × 2 hours, not 2 CU × 720 hours.

## Neon pricing examples

Side project (scale-to-zero, 1 GB RAM, 50 active hours): 0.25 CU × 50 hours × $0.106 + 0.5 GB storage × $0.35 = $1.50/month.

Startup SaaS (always-on, 1 vCPU / 4 GB RAM): 1 CU × 720 hours × $0.106 + 5 GB storage × $0.35 = $78.07/month.

sources.title: New 70s themed holiday bar opens in Savannah | The State
sources.snippet_text:
After the holiday bar closes, the property will undergo renovations ahead of Good Night John Boy's planned early 2027 opening. According to the announcement, the finished nightclub is expected to feature DJs, dancing, cocktails, entertainment and a design inspired by the 1970s.

The concept takes its name from the television series "The Waltons." Its locations feature elements including wood paneling, retro wallpaper, shag carpeting, neon and disco balls. [...] The temporary holiday bar features seasonal decorations, displays and holiday music, according to the announcement. Its menu includes holiday cocktails inspired by drinks served at Xmas Bar locations in other markets.

Some cocktails are also available to-go through a walk-up Grinch Bar.

More information about the concept is available at xmasbar.com.

The pop-up serves as an introduction to Good Night John Boy before construction begins on the permanent Savannah location. [...] The 1970s-inspired bar, restaurant and nightclub will eventually take over 301 W. Congress St., according to a community announcement. The Savannah location is expected to make its official debut in early 2027 after the holiday pop-up ends and renovations are completed.

sources.title: Visual Studio BYOM vs Copilot's Default Models: What Actually Changes? - DEV Community
sources.snippet_text:
Two announcements landed on November 10 and 11, 2026. First, Microsoft said Copilot Chat in Visual Studio 2026 version 18.12 now uses the Microsoft Copilot SDK and shared Copilot harness. The update is on by default. Second, BYOM became generally available in the same Visual Studio version, allowing developers to connect models from supported providers, custom endpoints, and local services. [...] The new experience also adds workflow features Microsoft describes as live steering, visible tool results, subagent activity cards, folder context beyond the solution, and built-in agents such as `/security-review` and `/rubber-duck`. The goal is for Copilot to continue through multiple steps and let a developer inspect what happened rather than receiving only a final summary.

`/security-review`
`/rubber-duck` [...] The GA release allows multiple named configurations for the same provider, such as separate work and personal endpoints. It also exposes API format selection for OpenAI-compatible Completions or Responses and Anthropic-compatible Messages. You can configure context size, maximum output, tool calling, and vision support to match the selected deployment.
